title: The Limits of Simulated Societies: How Post-Training and Survey Fine-Tuning Erase Cross-Cultural Variance

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing dispersion retention (deviation ratio) and point accuracy of simulated survey responses across WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic) and non-WEIRD populations using value-encoded personas from the World Values Survey.

Disaggregating prediction error and response spread (deviation ratio) across 12 specific countries to evaluate how model post-training and alignment disproportionately erase within-country diversity for underrepresented nations (e.g., Nigeria, Ethiopia).

Measuring 'consensus collapse' using Wasserstein-1 distance and deviation ratio to evaluate how LLMs flatten rich within-group demographic diversity into monolithic stereotypes, particularly converging on normatively 'correct' responses for sensitive questions.
